{
  "analysis": "The training data reveals that German legal texts frequently use specific titles (Dr., Mag., Univ.-Prof., etc.) and honorifics (Herr, Frau) as strong anchors for person names. The main challenge is handling complex academic titles and suffixes (e.g., 'Bakk. iur.', 'LLM') attached to names, as well as distinguishing between judges, parties, and representatives based on context like 'durch den Richter' or 'vertreten durch'.",
  "strategy": "Use a set of prioritized regex rules that anchor on specific German legal titles and honorifics to capture the full name string, including suffixes and middle names, while using negative lookaheads to avoid matching common nouns or addresses.",
  "note": "Every rule includes output_template and output_key. Patterns use capture groups for the name part to ensure precise extraction when context is needed, though full match is often sufficient for the name itself.",
  "rules": [
    {
      "name": "Academic and Professional Titles",
      "description": "Captures names preceded by complex academic titles like Dr., Mag., Univ.-Prof., Priv.-Doz., etc., including suffixes like Bakk. iur., LLM.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:Dr\\.|Mag\\.|Univ\\.-Prof\\.|Univ\\.-Prof\\.in|Priv\\.-Doz\\.|Priv\\.-Doz\\.in|Hon\\.-Prof\\.|MedR|KommR|Ing\\.|Bakk\\. iur\\.|LLM|BSc|RA\\.?|StB\\.?|Gf-?)(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)?\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*(?:\\s+(?:BSc|LLM|B\\.iur\\.|i\\.iur\\.))?)(?:,\\s*[A-Z][a-z]+)?",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 10,
      "reasoning": "High priority rule to catch the most common pattern in legal texts: titles followed by full names. Handles variations like 'Dr.', 'Mag.', 'Univ.-Prof.in' and suffixes."
    },
    {
      "name": "Honorifics Herr/Frau",
      "description": "Captures names preceded by 'Herr' or 'Frau' which are common in legal descriptions of parties.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:Herr|Frau)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 9,
      "reasoning": "Covers cases where titles are omitted but honorifics are used, ensuring names like 'Herr Möbs' or 'Frau Mag. GF1' are caught."
    },
    {
      "name": "Richter/Richterin Context",
      "description": "Specifically targets judges mentioned after 'durch den Richter' or 'durch die Richterin'.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:durch den Richter|durch die Richterin)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*(?:\\s+(?:Dr\\.?|Mag\\.?))?)(?:\\s+in)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 8,
      "reasoning": "Disambiguates judges from other parties by looking for the specific phrase 'durch den Richter' followed by a name."
    },
    {
      "name": "Representative Context",
      "description": "Captures names of representatives mentioned after 'vertreten durch'.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:vertreten durch)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*(?:\\s+(?:Dr\\.?|Mag\\.?))?)(?:,|\\s+[A-Z])",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 7,
      "reasoning": "Targets the 'vertreten durch' pattern which is very common for lawyers/representatives in these documents."
    },
    {
      "name": "Anonymous/Initial Names",
      "description": "Captures anonymized names like 'Dr. X.Y.' or 'Herr M.' found in redacted sections.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:Dr\\.|Herr|Frau)\\s+([A-Z]\\.[A-Z]\\.)|(?:Herr|Frau)\\s+([A-Z]\\.)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1$2",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 6,
      "reasoning": "Handles cases where names are redacted to initials, which appear frequently in legal training data."
    },
    {
      "name": "Simple First Name Only (Contextual)",
      "description": "Captures single capitalized words that appear in specific contexts like 'des Herrn [Name]' or 'der Frau [Name]'.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:des Herrn|der Frau)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 5,
      "reasoning": "Catches cases where only a first name is mentioned with a possessive honorific, e.g., 'des Herrn Gerrit'."
    }
  ],
  "deleted_rules": []
}

{
  "analysis": "The current rules fail because they capture only the last word of a multi-word name (e.g., 'Dok' instead of 'Dr. Dok2') or match partial words (e.g., 'Ost' from 'OstLextraMedien') due to lack of strict word boundaries and context anchoring.   "strategy": "Replace the broad 'Academic and Professional Titles' rule with a strict pattern that requires a title followed by a full name (First + Last) with word boundaries, and add specific rules for complex titles (e.g., ÖkR, Dipl.-Ing.) and anonymized initials to ensure only valid person entities are captured.",

      "description": "Captures names preceded by academic titles (Dr., Mag., Univ.-Prof., etc.) ensuring the full name is captured with strict word boundaries to avoid partial matches.",

      "priority": 10,
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$0",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "content": "\\b(?:Dr\\.|Mag\\.|Univ\\.-Prof\\.|Univ\\.-Prof\\.in|Priv\\.-Doz\\.|Priv\\.-Doz\\.in|Hon\\.-Prof\\.|MedR|KommR|Ing\\.|Bakk\\. iur\\.|LLM|BSc|RA\\.?|StB\\.?|Gf-?)(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)?\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*(?:\\s+(?:BSc|LLM|B\\.iur\\.|i\\.iur\\.)?)?)\\b"
    },
    {
      "name": "Complex Legal Titles",
      "description": "Specifically targets complex legal titles like ÖkR, Dipl.-Ing., StR, etc., which often precede names in German legal texts.",
      "format": "regex",
      "priority": 9,
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$0",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "content": "\\b(?:ÖkR|Dipl\\. -Ing\\.|Dipl\\. Kff\\. StR|StR|Mag\\. a|Mag\\. \\u00d6kR)(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*)\\b"
    },
    {
      "name": "Honorifics Herr/Frau",
      "description": "Captures names preceded by 'Herr' or 'Frau' but requires a full name (at least two words or a known pattern) to avoid matching partial words like 'Ost'.",
      "format": "regex",
      "priority": 8,
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$0",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "content": "\\b(?:Herr|Frau)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)+)\\b"
    },
    {
      "name": "Anonymous/Initial Names",
      "description": "Captures anonymized names like 'Dr. X.Y.' or 'Herr M.' but strictly requires the pattern to be followed by a space or punctuation to avoid matching 'R.' in 'Frau R.'.",
      "format": "regex",
      "priority": 6,
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$0",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "content": "\\b(?:Dr\\.|Herr|Frau)\\s+([A-Z]\\.[A-Z]\\.)\\b|\\b(?:Herr|Frau)\\s+([A-Z]\\.)\\b(?=\\s|$)"
    },
    {
      "name": "Simple First Name Only (Contextual)",
      "description": "Captures single capitalized words in specific contexts like 'des Herrn [Name]' but ensures the word is followed by a space or punctuation to avoid partial matches.",
      "format": "regex",
      "priority": 5,
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$0",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "content": "\\b(?:des Herrn|der Frau)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+)\\b(?=\\s|$)"
    }
  ],
  "deleted_rules": [
    "Academic and Professional Titles",
    "Honorifics Herr/Frau",
    "Anonymous/Initial Names",
    "Simple First Name Only (Contextual)"
  ]
}

WHAT MAKES A GOOD RULE:
- PRECISION OVER RECALL: A rule that matches 10 things correctly beats one that matches 100 with 20 wrong. Never sacrifice precision for recall. Missing a match is fixable later; a wrong match poisons results.
- GENERALIZE, DON'T MEMORIZE: Rules run on unseen text. Match the *structure* of values, not the exact strings you see in training data.
- USE CONTEXT: The same string can mean different things. Match surrounding words/punctuation and use capture groups ($1) to extract just the value.
- ONE RULE, ONE PATTERN: Multiple focused rules beat one giant regex. Each rule should have a clear, testable reason to exist.
- THINK ADVERSARIALLY: Before writing a rule, ask "what else could this match?" If the answer isn't empty, narrow the pattern or add context.

- \b word boundaries, (?:...) non-capturing groups, (a|b|c) alternation
- [A-Z] [a-z] \d \s character classes, +*?{n,m} quantifiers
- (?=...) lookahead, (?<=...) lookbehind — match context without consuming it
- (?i) case-insensitive flag

CAPTURE GROUPS ($1) vs FULL MATCH ($0):
- Use $0 in output_template when the entire regex match IS the value you want.
- Use $1 when you need surrounding context to disambiguate — put the value in a capture group.
  With "text": "$1", $start/$end auto-adjust to the group position automatically.

GOOD vs BAD PATTERNS (learn from these):

  BAD:  "\d+"                       — matches every number in the text, most will be wrong type
  GOOD: "(\d+)\s*(?:kg|lbs|oz)"    — only numbers followed by weight units; $1 captures the number

  GOOD: "(?:Mr|Mrs|Dr)\.?\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*)" — captures names after titles

  GOOD: "(?:in|from|at|near)\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*)" — locations after prepositions

  GOOD: "(?:email|contact)[:\s]+(\S+@\S+\.\w{2,})" — emails after a label; $1 captures address

WHAT MAKES A GOOD RULE:
